doc.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022

title: Joy and humor in playing with Anthony Braxton
summary: She says playing Braxton's quartet music was tremendous fun, purely about the music; reviews praise her on Braxton recordings.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I was watching a video of you and I was going to do this later but it seems relevant, with Anthony Braxton in Germany in a quartet setting. And as I watched I wondered if the emotion of joy and/or humor is possible in the kind of music you were playing because it seemed really intense and the concentration involved indicated perhaps that this was not fun.
Well I’m glad you said that because I hoped to be corrected.

Yeah, some of the most fun I’ve ever had playing. I mean Anthony is an amazing chess player. I think he even used to make a living playing chess in Washington Square Park. I might have dreamed that up but I think that’s true. And playing his music, it was a challenge but it was a fun challenge, you know? And you definitely had to be on your toes all the time. But there was a lot of joy and humor and it was really, I think when we were — at least speaking for myself — when we were doing this we weren’t thinking oh this is joyful, this is funny, this is angry. It was just about the music, purely about the music. And then these other things you sort of maybe notice as an afterthought.
Well when you stood up to take a bow you were all smiling.
It makes me think of another CD book, The Penguin Guide to Jazz I looked up Anthony Braxton and it said: “If Marilyn Crispell is on it buy it.”
